timed_text.text: A19, today we do something different.
There's a moment in your competitive career
where your mind completely broke on you.
Your focus left, the spiral started.
You couldn't come back.
And the performance suffered because of it.
You've probably replayed that moment as a failure.
What if you replayed it as a training opportunity instead?
You cannot achieve greatness without mistakes.
The question isn't whether you make errors.
Bill Bezick puts it this way.
You cannot achieve greatness without mistakes.
The question isn't whether you make errors.
The question is whether you're big enough to accept them,
learn from them, and refuse to let them define you.
That's what we're doing today.
Retrospective reframing.
Not pretending that bad moments didn't happen.
Updating your brain's response to it
with the tools you now have.
Every time you do this, that memory loses a little more
of its charge.
And the next time something similar happens in competition,
your brain looks for the train response,
not the old panic pattern.
Think of a specific moment.
One that still has some weight to it.
This caused you a lot of pain, a lot of anguish.
Oh, next on your screen, you're going to walk right through it.

cards.prompt: Describe the moment — the situation, what happened, what your mind did, and how it affected your performance.
At what exact point did the spiral begin? What was the first thought that started the chain?
With the tools you have now — your reset word, your reset protocol, your focus anchor, your If-Then plan — what would you have done differently? Walk through it step by step.
